sections.relationship: Students compare words by eye and miss a letter. Writing each word's letters in alphabetical order turns "is it an anagram?" into "are these strings equal?".
sections.author_note: Students compare words by eye and miss a letter. Writing each word's letters in alphabetical order turns "is it an anagram?" into "are these strings equal?".

lesson.title: Sort the letters
text: Write the letters of each word in alphabetical order, keeping repeats.
Two words are anagrams exactly when their sorted letters match.
To check whether a word can be spelled from a set of letters, cross off each letter as you use it.

example.title: Worked example (different words)
prompt: Are DIRTY and DIRT anagrams? Are CAFE and FACE?
steps: DIRTY sorts to D, I, R, T, Y and DIRT sorts to D, I, R, T. DIRTY has an extra Y, so they are not anagrams.
CAFE and FACE both sort to A, C, E, F: anagrams.
